questions.prompt: Which register is the 8051's 16-bit data pointer?
questions.explanation: DPTR is the 16-bit data pointer; SP tracks the stack and PC tracks instruction execution.

questions.prompt: What is the key distinction between MOVC and MOVX?
options: MOVC reads code memory; MOVX accesses external data memory.
MOVC writes a port; MOVX clears a bit.
They are interchangeable names for register moves.
MOVC returns from an interrupt; MOVX calls a subroutine.
questions.answer: MOVC reads code memory; MOVX accesses external data memory.
questions.explanation: The instructions address different memory spaces; whether external memory is available depends on the device.

questions.prompt: Why must an 8051-compatible derivative's datasheet be checked?
options: Compatible derivatives may differ in memory, peripherals, pins, and timing.
All derivatives have identical memory and timing.
The datasheet only lists the package color.
Assembly instructions do not depend on the target device.
questions.answer: Compatible derivatives may differ in memory, peripherals, pins, and timing.
questions.explanation: The 8051 name covers many implementations, so device-specific electrical and architectural details matter.
